ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass — computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder may not reject zero price when minSqrtPriceX96 == 0
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: validateHandlerOrder at AMMStandardHook.sol:215 calls computeRatioX96 and checks bounds. If sqrtPriceX96 == 0, the min bound check (line 218) catches it when minSqrtPriceX96 > 0. When minSqrtPriceX96 == 0 (not set), zero passes but no profit path exists because CLOB order execution uses the order's actual sqrtPriceX96 parameter (not the computed ratio). The pricing bounds validation is a safety check, not the execution price. Additionally, _enforcePriceBounds in the direct swap path (line 847) explicitly reverts on sqrtPriceX96 == 0.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call — calling CLOBTransferHandler fill path directly bypasses AMM hook pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.handleTransferCallback (line 230) requires msg.sender == AMM. Direct calls revert with CLOBTransferHandler__CallbackMustBeFromAMM. Similarly, afterSwapRefund (line 316) checks msg.sender == AMM. The only non-AMM-gated functions are openOrder/closeOrder/depositToken/withdrawToken, which manage orders and balances but do not execute swaps. No bypass path exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — CLOBTransferHandler.setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.setTokenSettings (line 376-378) creates memSettings from input, explicitly sets initialized=true (line 377), stores to _tokenSettings[token] (line 378), and syncs all hooks via registryUpdateTokenSettings (line 396-398). The CLOB reads token settings from the AMM (ILimitBreakAMM.getTokenSettings), not from its own storage. No independent setTokenSettings exists in CLOBTransferHandler. Settings flow is unidirectional: Registry → AMM → CLOB reads on demand.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT written in beforeSwap but not cleared after afterSwap read
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known by-design pattern (audit memory FP #1). Transient storage is automatically cleared at end of each transaction. Within a transaction, beforeSwap writes the slot (line 839) and afterSwap reads it (line 843-844). The AMM calls beforeSwap per-token, so the second call intentionally overwrites the first. No cross-swap staleness possible because the beforeSwap→afterSwap sequence is enforced by the AMM's swap flow. This is documented as HOOK-001 in the audit memory.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput rounds UP output (favors maker) — potential for maker to extract dust via many small fills
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Confirmed: CLOB uses mulDivRoundingUp for output, giving maker up to 4 wei more per fill than exact calculation. Over 100 fills at 1.75:1 price, cumulative overpayment was 207 wei. This is bounded by 4 * numFills wei total. At $3000/ETH, extracting $1 would require >10^14 fills — economically impossible due to gas costs. Not exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity line 69 operator precedence bug — redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0 may misparse
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Confirmed NOT a bug via solc bytecode analysis. Solidity's type system forces (uint256 | uint256) == uint256 interpretation because uint256 | bool is a type error. Both expressions compile to identical opcodes: OR then EQ. Verified by compiling with solc 0.8.16 and comparing bytecode.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: FixedHelper.sol:69 — solc bytecode verified identical for both interpretations

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction via 100+ tiny swaps on FixedPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FixedHelper rounds DOWN output (user gets less). With 1-wei swaps at 3:2 ratio, output rounds to 0 — pool gains 1 wei per swap. Over 100 iterations, pool balance only increases. Fuzz test C23 confirms no profitable round-trip possible. C24 confirms 1-wei sequential swaps never decrease pool balance.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Round-trip profit on DynamicPoolType via tick boundary manipulation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test (25 runs) confirms A→B→A always returns A_final <= A_initial. Fee deduction + rounding down output ensures no profit path. SwapMath.computeSwapByInputStep rounds fee UP (user pays more) and amount out DOWN (user gets less). Medusa ran 422,602 calls with 0 failures.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SingleProviderHelper round-trip profit via price precision loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test C20 confirms: forward (mulDiv roundDown) then reverse (mulDiv roundDown) always returns recoveredInput <= inputAmount. Two rounds of rounding down compound the loss. No profit possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee monotonicity violation — larger amounts could produce disproportionately small fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test C25 confirms fee is monotonically non-decreasing with amount for both input and output paths. mulDivRoundingUp(amount, feeBPS, MAX_BPS) is monotonic in amount when feeBPS and MAX_BPS are constant.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: uint128 truncation in DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed could lose accrued fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The cast uint128(mulDiv(feeGrowthDelta, liquidity, Q128)) is bounded because feeGrowthDelta is per-unit-of-liquidity and accumulated over actual swap volume. In practice, exceeding uint128 for tokensOwed would require impossibly large accumulated fees. Test C8 verifies the truncation behavior at extreme inputs.

theft_theses.thesis: Extract dust via repeated tiny CLOB fills exploiting mulDivRoundingUp overpayment
Profitable round-trip swap on FixedPoolType exploiting rounding direction
Profitable round-trip swap on DynamicPoolType via tick boundary crossing
Bypass pricing bounds via computeRatioX96 overflow returning 0
Operator precedence bug in FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity allows bypassing position-clearing safety check
Fee truncation at 1 BPS on small amounts gives free swaps
SingleProvider round-trip profit via accumulated precision loss across two price conversions
